source.title: The global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for unitary groups. II. From Eisenstein series to Bessel periods
readSections: The published version, read in full: the open-access (CC BY 4.0) PDF from Cambridge Core (98 pages; SHA-256 cf4d67e66276bdca486856754dcda7cddaeef75ed77d9924cd58c239de866439; fetched 23 September 2026; received 2 March 2025, accepted 28 March 2025). Read: §1 (Theorems 1.2.3.1, 1.2.4.1, 1.3.3.1, 1.3.6.1), §2 (preliminaries and Arthur's partition), §3 (the unitary Jacquet–Rallis trace formula and its (U, U′)-regular contribution), §4 (the (G, H)-regular contribution on the linear side and its Whittaker form), §5 (intertwining periods and Whittaker functions), §6 (the alternative proof via Flicker–Rallis zeta integrals), §7 (the comparison and the proofs of Theorems 1.2.3.1 and 1.2.4.1), §8 (reduction of Bessel periods to corank one, with the unramified computation), Appendix A (Weyl's character formula for non-connected groups) and the references. Page numbers are the journal's; misprints were checked on page images.
arXiv 2302.12331 has only v1 (23 February 2023); the 2025 published version, which thanks P. Boisseau for correcting the statement of Proposition 8.7.2.1 in a previous version, is the one extracted.

Cited inputs (Zydor, Chaudouard–Zydor, Ichino–Yamana 2015 and 2019, Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski, Lapid, Chaudouard 2022, Flicker, Feigon–Lapid–Offen, Beuzart-Plessis, Y. Liu, Khoury, L. Zhang, Mok, KMSW, Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry, Atiyah–Bott) were not read; items resting on them state them as the paper uses them. The use of Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu Theorem 4.14 was checked against its source (arXiv 1912.07169v3).

summary: The sequel to PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22. It extends the global Gan–Gross–Prasad and Ichino–Ikeda conjectures for U(n) × U(n+1) to periods of Eisenstein series attached to H-regular Hermitian Arthur parameters — parameters with a non-discrete part Π_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ Π_r ⊠ Π_0 ⊠ Π*_r ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ Π*_1 — and proves them (Theorems 1.2.3.1, 1.2.4.1). By a global and local unfolding with an unramified computation, it deduces the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture and Liu's refined (Ichino–Ikeda) conjecture for Bessel periods of U(m) × U(n+1) in general (Theorems 1.3.3.1, 1.3.6.1). The new spectral contributions are continuous: on the unitary side J^U_χ = ∫ J^U_{P,π}(λ) dλ through Ichino–Yamana regularised periods (§3); on the linear side I_χ = 2^{−dim 𝔞_L}∫ I_{P,π}(λ) dλ through general Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski intertwining periods and Chaudouard's spectral expansion of the Flicker–Rallis period (§4), expressed in Whittaker terms by a new formula for a basic intertwining period (Theorem 5.5.1.1) and reproved with zeta integrals (§6). All of it extends pending candidates, which this extraction coalesces with: the Jacquet–Rallis comparison, the Asai and Flicker–Rallis periods Part II, the Gan–Gross–Prasad framework and the Schwartz-function Part II. The one new owner is a small Part II of Tau Ceti's Lie groups roadmap for Weyl's character formula on non-connected groups ^LG = Ĝ ⋊ Γ (Appendix A). Eleven source issues are recorded; the one of substance (E1) is again the use of Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu Theorem 4.14(4) for a non-cuspidal base change.

items.name: Discrete and regular Hermitian Arthur parameters of G_n and the space 𝔞*_{Π,ℂ}
items.statement: A discrete Hermitian Arthur parameter of G_n = Res_{E/F} GL_n is Π ≅ Ind^{G_n}_Q(Π_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ Π_r) with Π_i conjugate self-dual cuspidal on G_{n_i}(A), mutually non-isomorphic, L(s, Π_i, As^{(−1)^{n+1}}) having a pole at s = 1; S_Π = (ℤ/2)^r. A regular Hermitian Arthur parameter is Π ≅ Ind^{G_n}_Q(Π_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ Π_r ⊠ Π_0 ⊠ Π*_r ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ Π*_1) with Levi G_{n_1} × ⋯ × G_{n_r} × G_{n_0} × G_{n_r} × ⋯ × G_{n_1} (n_0 + 2Σn_i = n), Π_0 a discrete Hermitian Arthur parameter of G_{n_0} (the discrete component, unique), Π_i cuspidal with central character trivial on A^∞, and Π_1, …, Π_r, Π*_1, …, Π*_r mutually non-isomorphic; S_Π = S_{Π_0}. With w the permutation swapping the blocks of Π_i and Π*_i, 𝔞*_{Π,ℂ} = {λ ∈ 𝔞*_{Q,ℂ} : wλ = −λ}, Π_λ = Ind((Π_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ Π*_1) ⊗ λ), irreducible for λ ∈ i𝔞*_Π. For G_n × G_{n′}: Π = Π_n ⊠ Π_{n′}, S_Π = S_{Π_n} × S_{Π_{n′}}, 𝔞*_{Π,ℂ} = 𝔞*_{Π_n,ℂ} × 𝔞*_{Π_{n′},ℂ}.
items.note: Extends the (discrete) Hermitian Arthur parameters that PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22 added to this candidate to parameters with a non-discrete part.

items.name: Weak base change of a cuspidal datum (P, σ) of a unitary group
items.statement: For h ∈ ℋ_n and a parabolic P ⊂ U(h) with M_P ≅ G_{n_1} × ⋯ × G_{n_r} × U(h_{n_0}) and σ = Π_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ Π_r ⊠ σ_0 cuspidal on M_P(A) (central character trivial on A^∞_P): a regular Hermitian Arthur parameter Π of G_n is a weak base change of (P, σ) if Π ≅ Ind^{G_n}_Q(Π_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ Π_r ⊠ Π_0 ⊠ Π*_r ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ Π*_1) for a discrete Hermitian Arthur parameter Π_0 of G_{n_0} with Π_{0,v} the split local base change of σ_{0,v} for almost all split v (Π_0 is then the weak base change of σ_0). Then 𝔞*_{P,ℂ} is identified with 𝔞*_{Π,ℂ} and Σ_λ = Ind^{U_h}_P(σ ⊗ λ); products U(h) × U(h′) are treated factorwise.
items.note: Extends the weak base change of cuspidal representations in this candidate to Eisenstein data.

items.name: H-regular Hermitian Arthur parameters of G_n × G_{n+1}
items.statement: Π = Π_n ⊠ Π_{n+1} with Π_k = Ind^{G_k}_{Q_k}(Π_{1,k} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ Π_{r_k,k}) is H-regular if Π_{i,n} ≄ Π^∨_{j,n+1} for all i, j. Remark 1.2.1.1: every discrete Hermitian Arthur parameter is H-regular, since otherwise some conjugate self-dual cuspidal Π_i would have poles at s = 1 of both L(s, Π_i, As^+) and L(s, Π_i, As^−).
items.note: The condition that makes the Rankin–Selberg L-function of Π pole-free and the regularised periods independent of truncation.

items.name: The Ichino–Ikeda L-value 𝓛(s, Σ_λ) and local normalised periods of induced tempered representations
items.statement: For σ tempered on M_P(A) with weak base change the regular Hermitian parameter Π and λ ∈ i𝔞*_Π: 𝓛(s, Σ_λ) = (s − ½)^{−dim 𝔞*_Π} ∏_{i=1}^{n+1} L(s + i − ½, η^i) L(s, Π_λ)/L(s + ½, Π_λ, As′), As′ = As^{(−1)^n} ⊠ As^{(−1)^{n+1}}; L(s, Π_λ, As′) has a pole of order dim 𝔞*_Π at s = 1, so (s − 1)^{dim 𝔞*_Π}L(s, Π_λ, As′) is holomorphic and non-zero at s = 1 and 𝓛(s, Σ_λ) is holomorphic at s = ½; 𝓛(s, Σ_λ) = (s − ½)^{−dim 𝔞*_Π}∏_v 𝓛(s, Σ_{λ,v}). P♮_{h,Σ_{λ,v}}(φ_v, φ′_v) = 𝓛(½, Σ_{λ,v})^{−1}∫_{U′_h(F_v)} (Σ_{λ,v}(h_v)φ_v, φ′_v)_v dh_v, absolutely convergent (Harris, Prop. 2.1), almost all factors 1 (Harris, Thm. 2.12).
items.note: Corrected statement: the paper prints (s − 1)^{−dim 𝔞*_Π}L(s, Π_λ, As′) (sourceIssues E2). Extends the candidate's P♮ (from PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22) to induced tempered representations.

items.name: Bessel data and global Bessel periods of U(m) × U(n+1)
items.statement: For n ≥ m ≥ 0 of the same parity, n = m + 2r: h_s = h_0 ⊕ (−h_0) with hyperbolic basis (x, y); for h ∈ ℋ_m, h̃ = h ⊕ h^1_s ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ h^r_s ∈ ℋ_n with hyperbolic pairs (x_i, y_i), h_{n+1} = h̃ ⊕ h_0 with v_0 ↔ 1 ∈ E; 𝒢_h = U(h) × U(h_{n+1}) with U(h) diagonal (acting trivially on h_0 ⊕ h^1_s ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ h^r_s); B ⊂ U(h_{n+1}) the stabiliser of the isotropic flag 0 ⊊ ⟨x_1⟩ ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ ⟨x_1, …, x_r⟩ with unipotent radical N, normalised by U(h); the Bessel subgroup ℬ_h = U(h) ⋉ ({1} × N); ψ_N(u) = ψ(Σ_{i=1}^{r−1} h_{n+1}(ux_{i+1}, y_i) + h_{n+1}(uv_0, y_r)) extended to ψ_{ℬ_h} trivial on U(h); for σ cuspidal on 𝒢_h(A), 𝒫_{ℬ_h,ψ}(φ) = ∫_{[ℬ_h]} φ(g)ψ_{ℬ_h}(g) dg (absolutely convergent). For m = 0 this is the Whittaker–Fourier coefficient of U_{2r+1}.
items.note: The unitary Bessel models and global Bessel periods of the candidate, in the coordinates the reduction of §8 uses.

items.name: Local Bessel periods on tempered functions and the refined conjecture for Bessel periods
items.statement: For G a reductive group over F_v, 𝒞^w(G(F_v)) = ∪_d 𝒞^w_d is the space of tempered functions (|L(X)R(Y)f| ≪ Ξ^G σ^d; Beuzart-Plessis, Astérisque 418, §1.5), containing C_c^∞ densely. f ↦ ∫_{U′(F_v)} f converges on 𝒞^w(U(F_v)) (BP20, Lemma 6.5.1) and f ↦ ∫_{ℬ(F_v)} f ψ_{ℬ,v} extends continuously to 𝒞^w(𝒢(F_v)) (BP20, Prop. 7.1.1), likewise the Whittaker and Whittaker–Bessel periods; for tempered σ_v and matrix coefficients, 𝒫_{ℋ,v}(φ_v, φ′_v) := 𝒫_{ℋ,v}(f_{φ_v,φ′_v}). With 𝓛(s, σ_v) = ∏_{i=1}^{n+1}L(s + i − ½, η^i_v) L(s, Π_v)/L(s + ½, Π_v, As′), As′ = As^{(−1)^m} ⊗ As^{(−1)^{n+1}}, the normalised local Bessel period is P♮_{ℬ_h,ψ_v} = 𝓛(½, σ_v)^{−1}𝒫_{ℬ_h,ψ,v}, and almost all normalised factors equal 1 (Y. Liu, Crelle 2016, Thm. 2.2). The refined conjecture (Liu, Conj. 2.5; for m = 0 Lapid–Mao, Conj. 1.1) is the identity of Theorem 1.3.6.1.
items.note: The refined (Ichino–Ikeda type) conjecture for Bessel periods is part of the candidate's framework; the analytic extension of the local periods is Beuzart-Plessis's.

items.name: Uniqueness of Bessel models and the factorisation of Whittaker–Bessel functionals
items.statement: Over a local field, Hom_{ℬ(F_v)}(σ, ψ_{ℬ,v}) has dimension at most one for irreducible σ of U_m × U_{n+1} (Aizenbud–Gourevitch–Rallis–Schiffmann; Gan–Gross–Prasad, Cor. 15.3; Jiang–Sun–Zhu); consequently every L ∈ Hom_{ℬ_L(F_v)}(τ ⊠ σ, ψ^L_{ℬ,v}) factors as L_W ⊗ L_B with L_W ∈ Hom_{N_r(F_v)}(τ, ψ_{−r,v}) and L_B ∈ Hom_{ℬ(F_v)}(σ, ψ_{ℬ,v}).
items.note: The multiplicity-one theorems are cited in the candidate's brief.

items.name: Unramified Bessel functions (Khoury; Liu; L. Zhang)
items.statement: For v ∉ S, unramified σ = σ_m ⊠ σ_{n+1} with regular Satake parameter S = (S_m, S_{n+1}) ∈ ^LT, spherical vectors normalised by L_B(φ°_m ⊗ φ°_{n+1}) = 1 and t ∈ Λ_r: L_B(φ°_m ⊗ σ_{n+1}(t)φ°_{n+1}) = (Δ^U_{m,v})^{−1}Σ_{w∈W(𝒢_v)} det(1 − q^{−1/2}R_−(wS))/D_{Ĝ/B̂}(wS) χ_t((wS_{n+1})^{(r)})δ_P(t)^{1/2} for t ∈ Λ^{++}_r and 0 otherwise (8.7.2.4), the Weyl sum extending to a regular function on ^LT; and (Δ^U_{m,v})^{−1}Σ_{w̃∈W(Ũ_v)} det(1 − q^{−1/2}R̃_−(w̃S̃))/D_{Ĝ/B̂}(w̃S̃) = 1 (Liu, Prop. 6.4).
items.note: Khoury (thesis 2008, Thm. 11.4), Liu (Crelle 2016, Prop. 6.4) and L. Zhang (Sci. China Math. 2018); the L-group notation (R, R_−, ⊗^I, As_m, ^LT) is that of §8.7.2.

items.name: The local Gan–Gross–Prasad theorem and the non-vanishing of the semi-local distribution
items.statement: For tempered σ_v supporting a non-zero U′_h(F_v)-invariant functional at every v ∈ S_0, the semi-local distribution ∏_{v∈S_0} J_{Σ_{λ,v}} does not vanish identically (BP20, Thm. 8.2.1); with Mok and KMSW's L-packets, only the term of σ survives in J^h_Π(λ, f^h) (local Gan–Gross–Prasad, BP20).
items.note: The tempered local conjecture for unitary groups, in this candidate through PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-LIU-ZHANG-ETAL-21.

items.name: Theorem 1.2.3.1: the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for Eisenstein series
items.statement: Let Π be an H-regular Hermitian Arthur parameter of G = G_n × G_{n+1} and λ ∈ i𝔞*_Π. Then L(½, Π_λ) ≠ 0 (complete L-function, archimedean places included) if and only if there are h ∈ ℋ_n, a parabolic P ⊂ U_h with Levi M_P and an irreducible cuspidal σ ⊂ 𝒜(M_P) such that Π is a weak base change of (P, σ) and φ ↦ 𝒫_{U′_h}(φ, λ) is a non-zero linear form on 𝒜_{P,σ}(U_h).
items.locator: Theorem 1.2.3.1 and Remark 1.2.3.2, p. 5; proof §7.2, pp. 69–70
items.note: For discrete Π (P = U_h) this is Theorem 1.1.5.1 of PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22, and Theorem 1.8 of Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu when Π is cuspidal. The proof rests on Theorem 7.1.6.1, whose Lemma 7.1.7.1 invokes BPLZZ Theorem 4.14(4) (sourceIssues E1).

items.name: Theorem 1.2.4.1: factorisation of periods of Eisenstein series à la Ichino–Ikeda
items.statement: Let Π and (P, σ) be as in §1.2.4 with σ tempered, λ ∈ i𝔞*_Π, Petersson product on 𝒜_{P,σ}(U_h) and periods normalised by Tamagawa measures, and local measures factorising the Tamagawa measure on U′_h(A). For every non-zero factorisable φ = ⊗′φ_v ∈ 𝒜_{P,σ}(U_h) ≃ ⊗′Σ_v: |𝒫_{U′_h}(φ, λ)|²/(φ, φ)_Pet = |S_Π|^{−1}𝓛(½, Σ_λ)∏_v P♮_{h,Σ_{λ,v}}(φ_v, φ_v)/(φ_v, φ_v)_v (1.2.4.1).
items.note: Reduces to Theorem 1.1.6.1 of PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22 for discrete Π.

items.name: Theorem 1.3.3.1: the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for Bessel periods of unitary groups
items.statement: Let Π be a discrete Hermitian Arthur parameter of G♭ = G_m × G_{n+1}. Then L(½, Π) ≠ 0 if and only if there are h ∈ ℋ_m and a cuspidal σ ⊂ 𝒜(𝒢_h) whose weak base change to G♭ is Π and on which the Bessel period 𝒫_{ℬ_h,ψ} does not vanish identically. For m = 0 this is Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry's Whittaker case; the direction (2) ⇒ (1) is also Jiang–Zhang (Thm. 5.7).
items.locator: Theorem 1.3.3.1 and Remarks 1.3.3.2, p. 7; reduction §1.3.4, pp. 7–8, and §8.8
items.note: Corrected statement: the paper prints G♭ = G_m × G_{2n+1} (sourceIssues E3). Deduced from Theorem 1.2.3.1 applied to Π̃ = Ind(α_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α_r ⊠ Π_m ⊠ α*_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ α*_r) ⊠ Π_{n+1} with unitary characters α_i and Proposition 8.8.2.1.

items.name: Theorem 1.3.6.1: the Ichino–Ikeda conjecture for Bessel periods (Liu's refined conjecture)
items.statement: Let σ ⊂ 𝒜_cusp(𝒢_h) be tempered everywhere with weak base change to G♭ a discrete Hermitian parameter Π, Petersson product and local measures normalised by Tamagawa measures on 𝒢_h(A) and ℬ_h(A). For every non-zero factorisable φ = ⊗′φ_v ∈ σ: |𝒫_{ℬ_h,ψ}(φ)|²/(φ, φ)_Pet = |S_Π|^{−1}𝓛(½, σ)∏_v P♮_{ℬ_h,ψ_v}(φ_v, φ_v)/(φ_v, φ_v)_v (1.3.6.1).
items.note: Conjectured by Y. Liu (Conj. 2.5) and, for m = 0, by Lapid–Mao; deduced from Theorem 1.2.4.1 through Proposition 8.8.3.1.

items.name: Arthur's partition of [G]_Q and the characteristic functions F^P(·, T)
items.statement: For T ∈ T_0 + 𝔞^{G,+}_0 and standard Q: Σ_{P_0⊂P⊂Q} Σ_{δ∈P(F)∖Q(F)} F^P(δg, T)τ^Q_P(H_P(δg) − T) = 1 (Arthur 1978, Lemma 6.4; Labesse–Waldspurger, Prop. 3.6.3), where F^P(·, T) is the characteristic function of ω_0A^{P,∞}_0(T_−, T)K, equivalently of {g ∈ [G]_P : ⟨ϖ, H_0(δg) − T⟩ ≤ 0 for all ϖ ∈ Δ̂^P_0, δ ∈ P(F)} (Arthur 1985, Lemma 2.1).
items.note: Arthur's truncation and partition (AS.3); Siegel domains are AA.3.

items.name: The weights d_Q(λ, g, T) built from Arthur's partition: Lemma 2.3.3.1, Proposition 2.3.4.1, Lemma 2.3.4.2, Proposition 2.3.4.3
items.statement: Lemma 2.3.3.1: if F^P(g, T)τ^Q_P(H_P(g) − T) = 1 then ⟨α, H_0(g)⟩ > ⟨α, T⟩ for α ∈ Δ^Q_0 ∖ Δ^P_0, and g ∈ 𝔰_P implies g ∈ 𝔰_Q. For φ: 𝔞_0 → ℂ, d_Q(φ, g, T) = Σ_{P⊂Q}Σ_{δ∈P(F)∖Q(F)} F^P(δg, T)τ^Q_P(H_P(δg) − T)e^{φ(H_P(δg))}. Proposition 2.3.4.1: e^{⟨λ,H_0(g)⟩} ∼ d_Q(λ, g, T) on 𝔰_Q uniformly for T in compacts, and d_Q(λ, gc, T) ∼ d_Q(λ, g, T) for c in a compact set — so d_Q(λ, ·, T) is a Franke weight. Lemma 2.3.4.2: for Q ⊂ R there is T_1 with d_Q(λ, g, T_0) = d_R(λ, g, T_0) whenever F^Q(g, T)τ^R_Q(H_Q(g) − T) = 1, T ∈ T_1 + 𝔞^{G,+}_0. Proposition 2.3.4.3: if Δ^R_0 ∖ Δ^Q_0 = {α} and c > ⟨α, T_{0,P}⟩ for all P ⊂ Q, then for each g at most one δ ∈ Q(F)∖R(F) has d_Q(α, δg, T_0) > e^c.
items.note: An explicit construction of the Franke weights of the candidate's function-space layer (after Franke, Prop. 2.1).

items.name: Lemma 3.5.6.1: spectral expansion of the kernel for a U-regular cuspidal datum
items.statement: For χ ∈ 𝔛(U) U-regular (the π′_i, (π′_i)* pairwise distinct, likewise for U″), any representative (M_P, π) and f ∈ 𝒮(U(A)): K_{f,χ}(x, y) = ∫_{i𝔞*_P} Σ_{φ∈ℬ_{P,π}} E(x, I_P(λ, f)φ, λ)\overline{E(y, φ, λ)} dλ, absolutely convergent; the space 𝒜^0_{Q,χ,disc}(U) is ⊕̂_{w∈W(P,Q)} 𝒜_{Q,wπ,cusp}(U) and Σ_Q |W(P, Q)|n_Q^{−1} = 1. Lemma 3.5.6.2 is the same with Λ^{T_1}_u and Λ^{T_2}_u on both variables, and (3.5.6.6) bounds the sums by truncated diagonal kernels via Cauchy–Schwarz (f = f_1 ∗ f_2^∗, Dixmier–Malliavin).
items.note: The regular-datum case of the candidate's Lemma 2.10.2.1 (PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22).

items.name: The unitary Jacquet–Rallis setup and Zydor's modified kernel K^T_{f,χ} on U = U′ × U″
items.statement: For h ∈ ℋ_n: U′_h = U(h), U″_h = U(h ⊕ h_0), U_h = U′_h × U″_h with U′_h ↪ U″_h (g ↦ diag(g, 1)) and U′_h diagonal in U_h; a minimal parabolic P′_0 of U′ (stabiliser of an isotropic flag), P″_0 ⊂ U″ stabilising the same flag, F′_0 → F_0, P′ ↦ P = P′ × P″ (3.1.4.1); good maximal compacts; Siegel domains of U = products (3.1.4.2); Proposition 3.1.5.1 compares d_{P″}(λ) and d_{P′}(λ) on [U′]_{P′}; T sufficiently positive. For f ∈ 𝒮(U(A)): K^T_{f,χ}(x, y) = Σ_{P′∈F′_0} ε_{P′}Σ_{γ,δ∈P′(F)∖U′(F)} τ̂_{P′}(H_{P′}(δy) − T)K_{f,P,χ}(γx, δy), ε_{P′} = (−1)^{dim 𝔞_{P′}}, absolutely convergent for Schwartz f (3.2.2.3).
items.note: Zydor's unitary kernel (Crelle 2020, §4) for Schwartz test functions.

items.name: Theorem 3.2.3.1: the coarse spectral expansion of the unitary Jacquet–Rallis trace formula for Schwartz functions
items.statement: For T sufficiently positive: (1) Σ_χ ∫_{[U′]×[U′]} |K^T_{f,χ}(x, y)| dx dy < ∞; (2) J^{U,T}_χ(f) = ∫_{[U′]×[U′]} K^T_{f,χ} is an exponential-polynomial in T whose purely polynomial part is a constant J^U_χ(f); (3) each J^U_χ is continuous and left and right U′(A)-invariant; (4) J^U(f) = Σ_χ J^U_χ(f) converges absolutely and is a continuous distribution.
items.note: Extends Zydor, Crelle 2020, Theorems 4.1, 4.5 and 4.7, from C_c^∞ to 𝒮(U(A)); the extension of Corollary 3.4.2.2 and Theorem 3.3.5.1(1) to the auxiliary kernels of Zydor's §4.1 is 'left to the reader' — a proof obligation. Chaudouard–Zydor already state the Schwartz extension.

items.name: The Ichino–Yamana truncation operator Λ^T_u for U(n) × U(n+1)
items.statement: For φ on [U] = [U′] × [U″] and x ∈ [U′]: (Λ^T_uφ)(x) = Σ_{P′∈F′_0} ε_{P′}Σ_{δ∈P′(F)∖U′(F)} τ̂_{P′}(H_{P′}(δx) − T)φ_{U′×P″}(δx), with φ_{U′×P″} the constant term along U′ × P″ evaluated diagonally. Proposition 3.3.3.1: φ ↦ Λ^T_uφ is continuous 𝒯([U]) → 𝒮_0([U′]), and |(Λ^T_uφ)(x) − F^{U′}(x, T)φ(x)| ≤ e^{−r‖T‖}‖x‖^{−N_2}_{U′}‖φ‖ for a continuous seminorm on 𝒯_{N_1}([U]) (Lemmas 3.3.3.2, 3.3.4.1). The truncation formula (Λ^{T+T′}_uφ)(x) = Σ_{R′}Σ_{δ} Γ_{R′}(H_{R′}(δx) − T_{R′}, T′)(Λ^{T,R′}_uφ)(δx) (3.5.3.3) (Ichino–Yamana, J. reine angew. Math. 2019, (2.2)).
items.note: Ichino–Yamana, Periods of automorphic forms: the case of (U_{n+1} × U_n, U_n) (2019), Lemma 2.2; the unitary counterpart of the linear Λ^T_r of PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22.

items.name: Theorem 3.3.5.1, Corollary 3.3.5.2, Theorem 3.4.2.1 and Corollary 3.4.2.2: J^U_χ from the truncated kernel
items.statement: (1) For T sufficiently positive, Σ_χ ∫_{[U′]×[U′]} |(K_{f,χ}Λ^T_u)(x, y)| ≤ ‖f‖ for a continuous seminorm on 𝒮(U(A)). (2) For every r > 0, Σ_χ |J^{U,T}_χ(f) − ∫(K_{f,χ}Λ^T_u)| ≤ e^{−r‖T‖}‖f‖; hence ∫_{[U′]×[U′]} (K_{f,χ}Λ^T_u) is asymptotic to an exponential-polynomial with constant term J^U_χ(f). Theorem 3.4.2.1: Σ_χ |K^T_{f,χ}(x, y) − K_{f,χ}(x, y)F^{U′}(y, T)| ≤ e^{−r‖T‖}‖x‖^{−N_1}‖y‖^{−N_2}‖f‖; Corollary 3.4.2.2: the same with K_{f,χ}Λ^T_u (Lemmas 3.4.5.1–3.4.5.2).
items.locator: Theorem 3.3.5.1, Corollary 3.3.5.2, §3.4, Theorem 3.4.2.1, Corollary 3.4.2.2, Lemmas 3.4.5.1–3.4.5.2, pp. 25–30
items.note: The new, independent characterisation of J^U_χ; the sums over χ ∈ 𝔛(U) are printed over 𝔛(G) (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: U-regular, U′-regular and (U, U′)-regular cuspidal data of U
items.statement: For χ = (χ′, χ″) ∈ 𝔛(U′) × 𝔛(U″) represented by M′ ≅ G_{n′_1} × ⋯ × G_{n′_{r′}} × U(h′), π′ = π′_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ π′_{r′} ⊠ σ′ (likewise for U″): χ is U-regular if π′_1, …, π′_{r′}, (π′_1)*, …, (π′_{r′})* are pairwise distinct and likewise for χ″; U′-regular if for n′_i = n″_j, (π′_i)^∨ and π″_j are neither isomorphic nor conjugate dual; (U, U′)-regular if both. If Π is an H-regular Hermitian Arthur parameter, the data of 𝔛^h_Π are (U, U′)-regular.
items.note: The unitary counterpart of the (G, H)-regular data of §4.1.3.

items.name: Proposition 3.5.3.1 and §3.5.4: the Ichino–Yamana regularised period of Eisenstein series on U_h
items.statement: For φ ∈ 𝒜_{P,π,cusp}(U) and λ regular for E(φ, λ), T sufficiently positive: (1) ∫_{[U′]} Λ^T_uE(x, φ, λ) dx converges absolutely; (2) if (M, π) is U′-regular it does not depend on T — this defines 𝒫_{U′}(φ, λ), meromorphic in λ, holomorphic where E(φ, λ) is (in particular on i𝔞*_P), continuous in φ; (3) if P′ = U′ or P″ = U″, then E(φ, λ)|_{[U′]} is rapidly decreasing and ∫_{[U′]} Λ^T_uE = ∫_{[U′]} E. Independence of T reduces via (3.5.3.3) to the vanishing (3.5.3.4) of truncated periods over [M_{R′}]^1, a product of Arthur-truncated Rankin inner products of GL-Eisenstein series and a smaller unitary operator, which vanish by Langlands's inner product formula and U′-regularity.
items.note: Ichino–Yamana's regularised period (2019), made independent of T under U′-regularity; the object in the statement of Theorem 1.2.3.1.

items.name: The unitary relative characters J^U_{P,π}(λ, f)
items.statement: For (M, π) U′-regular and f ∈ 𝒮(U(A)): J^U_{P,π}(λ, f) = Σ_{φ∈ℬ_{P,π}} 𝒫_{U′}(I_P(λ, f)φ, λ)\overline{𝒫_{U′}(φ, λ)} (3.5.5.1), absolutely convergent outside the singularities, holomorphic on i𝔞*_P, independent of the K-basis and continuous in f. Proposition 3.5.5.1: J^U_{P,π}(λ, f) = J^U_{P_1,π_1}(w·λ, f) for w ∈ W(M, M_1) with π_1 = wπ.
items.note: Continuity by PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22's Proposition 2.8.4.1 (printed '2.8.41', sourceIssues E10).

items.name: Proposition 3.5.6.4 and Theorem 3.5.7.1: the (U, U′)-regular contribution is an integral of relative characters
items.statement: There is a continuous seminorm with Σ_{(M,π)} ∫_{i𝔞*_P} |J^U_{P,π}(λ, f)| dλ ≤ ‖f‖, the sum over representatives of (U, U′)-regular data. For χ ∈ 𝔛(U) (U, U′)-regular and any representative (M_P, π): J^U_χ(f) = ∫_{i𝔞*_P} J^U_{P,π}(λ, f) dλ, absolutely convergent (= (1.4.2.2)).
items.note: Proof: integrate Lemma 3.5.6.2 over [U′] × [U′] (both truncations), let T_1 → ∞ by dominated convergence, and use Corollary 3.3.5.2. The contribution is continuous, in contrast with the discrete linear-side contribution of PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22.

items.name: (G, H)-regular and Hermitian cuspidal data of G_n × G_{n+1} and the Levi L ⊃ M
items.statement: For χ = (χ_n, χ_{n+1}) represented by M_j = G_{n_{1,j}} × ⋯ × G_{n_{r_j,j}}, π_j = σ_{1,j} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ σ_{r_j,j}: χ is G-regular if σ_{i,j} = σ_{i′,j} with n_{i,j} = n_{i′,j} forces i = i′; H-regular if σ_{i,n} ≄ σ^∨_{j,n+1} when n_{i,n} = n_{j,n+1}; (G, H)-regular if both; Hermitian if π = π* and σ_{i,j} is η_{G′_j}-distinguished whenever σ_{i,j} = σ*_{i,j}. For such χ one orders the blocks so that σ_{i+1,j} = σ*_{i,j} ≠ σ_{i,j} for odd i < 2s_j and σ_{i,j} = σ*_{i,j} for i > 2s_j, sets L_j = G_{n_{1,j}+n_{2,j}} × ⋯ × G_{n_{2s_j−1,j}+n_{2s_j,j}} × G_{n_{2s_j+1,j}} × ⋯ (4.1.4.1), ξ ∈ W(M) the involution with 𝔞^L_M = ker(ξ + 1) and Q ⊃ P with Levi L. Π = Ind^G_P(π) is then an H-regular Hermitian Arthur parameter, and |S_Π| = 2^{dim 𝔞_L − dim 𝔞^L_M} (7.1.4.1).
items.note: Extends the ∗-regular relevant data of PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22 to data with conjugate pairs.

items.name: Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski intertwining periods J(ξ, φ, λ) and their parabolic descent
items.statement: For ξ̃ ∈ L(F) with ξ̃c(ξ̃)^{−1} = ξ: P_ξ̃ = G′ ∩ ξ̃^{−1}Pξ̃ = M_ξ̃N_ξ̃ (N_ξ̃ = N_{Q′}, A^∞_{M_ξ̃} = A^∞_L), and for φ ∈ 𝒜_{P,π}(G), λ ∈ 𝔞^{L,*}_{M,ℂ}: J(ξ, φ, λ) = ∫_{A^∞_{M_ξ̃}M_ξ̃(F)N_ξ̃(A)∖G′(A)} e^{⟨λ,H_P(ξ̃h)⟩}φ(ξ̃h)η_{G′}(h) dh, a right G′(A)-invariant form on (N_ξ̃(A)A^∞M_ξ̃(F), δ_{P,ξ̃})-equivariant functions, convergent for ⟨λ, α^∨⟩ ≫ 0 (α^∨ ∈ Δ^{Q,∨}_P), meromorphic in λ, independent of ξ̃ (Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski, Thm. 23, Lemma 32); J_L(ξ, ·, λ) likewise on L. Lemma 4.1.5.1: J(ξ, φ, λ) = J_L(ξ, φ^{K′}, λ) with φ^{K′}(g) = e^{−⟨ρ_Q,H_Q(g)⟩}∫_{K′} φ(gk′)η_{G′}(k′) dk′; by Lapid 2006, Lemma 8.1 case 2, this equals ∫_{[L′]_0} Λ^T_mE^Q(x, φ^{K′}, λ)η_{G′}(x) dx (4.1.5.6), so J(ξ, ·, λ) is holomorphic and continuous on i𝔞^{L,*}_M.
items.note: The general intertwining periods of Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski, beyond the case ξ = 1 used by PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22.

items.name: The Rankin–Selberg period of Eisenstein series for H-regular data and the relative character I_{P,π}(λ, f)
items.statement: For (M, π) H-regular and λ ∈ 𝔞*_M: 𝒫(E(φ, λ)) = ∫_{[H]} Λ^T_rE(h, φ, λ) dh, independent of T (as in PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22, Prop. 5.1.4.1), holomorphic on i𝔞*_M and continuous in φ. For (G, H)-regular Hermitian χ and λ ∈ i𝔞^{L,*}_M: I_{P,π}(λ, f) = Σ_{φ∈ℬ_{P,π}} 𝒫(E(I_P(λ, f)φ, λ))·\overline{J(ξ, φ̄, −λ)}, and f ↦ (λ ↦ I_{P,π}(λ, f)) is continuous 𝒮(G(A)) → 𝒮(i𝔞^{L,*}_M) (Lapid 2006, Prop. 6.1; Chaudouard 2022, Prop. 7.2.3.2).
items.note: The relative character on the linear side of the comparison.

items.name: Chaudouard's spectral expansion of the Flicker–Rallis period of the kernel
items.statement: For the symmetric space GL_n(E)/GL_n(F), the Flicker–Rallis period ∫_{[G′]_0}∫_{A^∞_G} K_χ(ax, g)η(g) da dg of the χ-part of the kernel has an explicit, absolutely convergent spectral expansion Σ_{P_1}|𝒫(M_1)|^{−1}Σ_{L_1∈ℒ_2(M_1)} 2^{−dim 𝔞_{L_1}}Σ ∫_{i𝔞^{L_1,*}_{M_1}} ℐ_{L_1,wπ}(x, f, λ) dλ in terms of Eisenstein series and intertwining periods (Chaudouard, A spectral expansion for the symmetric space GL_n(E)/GL_n(F), arXiv:2204.06069, Thm. 7.2.4.1, Prop. 7.2.3.2).
items.note: A cited input, stated as the paper uses it for a product of two linear groups with the η_{G′}-twist; its general statement belongs with the Flicker–Rallis periods.

items.name: Lemma 4.1.9.1: the Flicker–Rallis period of the kernel for a (G, H)-regular datum
items.statement: For χ (G, H)-regular and x ∈ G(A), ∫_{[G′]} K_χ(x, g)η_{G′}(g) dg (absolutely convergent) vanishes unless χ is Hermitian; if χ is Hermitian and represented by (M_P, π): ∫_{[G′]} K_χ(x, g)η_{G′}(g) dg = 2^{−dim 𝔞_L}∫_{i𝔞^{L,*}_M} Σ_{φ∈ℬ_{P,π}} E(x, I_P(λ, f)φ, λ)·\overline{J(ξ, φ̄, −λ)} dλ (4.1.9.4).
items.note: From Chaudouard's Theorem 7.2.4.1, the factor 2^{−dim 𝔞_G} of the measures on A^∞_G and A^∞_{G′}, the identities (4.1.9.7)–(4.1.9.8) (functional equations of Eisenstein series and of intertwining periods, JLR Thm. 31 with Lapid 2006, Lemma 8.1) and Σ_{P_1}|𝒫(M_1)|^{−1}|W(P, P_1)| = 1.

items.name: Theorem 4.1.8.1: the (G, H)-regular contribution to the linear Jacquet–Rallis trace formula
items.statement: Let χ ∈ 𝔛(G) be (G, H)-regular. (1) If χ is not Hermitian, I_χ = 0. (2) If χ is Hermitian, with (M_P, π) and L as in §4.1.4: I_χ(f) = 2^{−dim 𝔞_L}∫_{i𝔞^{L,*}_M} I_{P,π}(λ, f) dλ for all f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)), absolutely convergent (4.1.8.1).
items.note: From the Λ^T_r characterisation of I_χ (PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22, Prop. 3.3.8.1 and Thm. 3.3.9.1), its Lemma 5.2.2.1, Lemma 4.1.9.1 and Fubini (Lapid 2006, Lemma 7.4). Extends Theorem 5.2.1.1 of PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22 (∗-regular, L = M) to conjugate pairs.

items.name: Propositions 4.2.5.1, 4.2.6.1 and 4.2.7.1: Whittaker expressions for the two periods
items.statement: For χ as in §4.1.4, λ ∈ i𝔞^{G,*}_P, Π_λ = Ind(π_λ) (irreducible, unitary, generic), W(g, φ, λ) = ∫_{[N]} E(ug, φ, λ)ψ_N(u)^{−1} du ∈ W(Π_λ, ψ_N): (4.2.5.1) Z^RS(0, W(φ, λ)) = 𝒫(E(φ, λ)) (Ichino–Yamana, Compositio 2015, Thm. 1.1, using H-regularity); (4.2.6.1) ⟨φ, φ⟩_Pet = ⟨W(φ, λ), W(φ, λ)⟩_Whitt (as PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22, Thm. 8.1.2.1, G-regularity); (4.2.7.1) J(ξ, φ, λ) = β_η(W(φ, λ)), via Lemma 4.1.5.1, W. Zhang's JAMS 2014 Prop. 3.2, Flicker, Theorem 5.5.1.1 and the local Theorem 9.1.7.1 of PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22, with Π^Q_λ (L′, η_{G′})-distinguished (Flicker 1992, Prop. 2.6) and L^{S,*}(1, Π^Q_λ, As_L)W^S = L^{S,*}(1, Π_λ, As)W (Shahidi 1981, §4).
items.note: Generalise Flicker's computation of Flicker–Rallis periods and the Ichino–Yamana Rankin–Selberg identity to G-regular Hermitian data.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.8.1: the Whittaker relative character I_{Π_λ} equals I_{P,π}(λ)
items.statement: For f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)) and λ ∈ i𝔞^{L,*}_M: I_{Π_λ}(f) = Σ_{φ∈ℬ_{P,π}} Z^RS(0, W(I_P(λ, f)φ, λ))\overline{β_η(W(φ, λ))}/⟨W(φ, λ), W(φ, λ)⟩_Whitt converges, is independent of ℬ_{P,π}, is a continuous distribution, and I_{Π_λ}(f) = I_{P,π}(λ, f).
items.locator: (4.2.8.1) and Theorem 4.2.8.1, p. 46; announced in §1.4.3, p. 11
items.note: Corrected statement: the denominators are printed ⟨·,·⟩_Pet (sourceIssues E7). Term-by-term from Propositions 4.2.5.1–4.2.7.1.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.2.1 (Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski): P(F)∖G(F)/G′(F) and twisted involutions
items.statement: For G = G_{2n}, P = MN with M = G_n × G_n: every double coset in P(F)∖G(F)/G′(F) has a representative ξ̃ with ξ = ξ̃c(ξ̃)^{−1} ∈ _PW_{P,2}, the involutions of _PW_P = {w : M ∩ w^{−1}B_{2n}w = M ∩ B_{2n} = M ∩ wB_{2n}w^{−1}}, and P(F)ξ̃G′(F) ↦ ξ is a bijection onto _PW_{P,2}. For ξ̃_0 = (I_n τI_n; I_n −τI_n) (τ^c = −τ), ξ_0 ∈ _PW_{P,2}, P_{ξ̃_0} = M_{ξ̃_0} and A^∞_{M_{ξ̃_0}} = A^∞_{G′}.
items.note: Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski, Prop. 20.

items.name: The basic intertwining period J(ξ_0, φ, λ) for π = σ ⊠ σ*
items.statement: For σ cuspidal on G_n with central character trivial on A^∞_{G_n}, π = σ ⊠ σ* and φ ∈ 𝒜_{P,π}(G): J(ξ_0, φ, λ) = ∫_{A^∞_{M_{ξ̃_0}}M_{ξ̃_0}(F)∖G′(A)} e^{⟨λ,H_P(ξ̃h)⟩}φ(ξ̃h) dh (5.1.3.1), absolutely convergent for Re⟨λ, α⟩ ≫ 0 and meromorphic on 𝔞^{G,*}_{P,ℂ} (Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski, Thm. 23).
items.note: The building block of Proposition 4.2.7.1.

items.name: Proposition 5.2.2.1: intertwining periods twisted by the Epstein series
items.statement: For Φ ∈ 𝒮(A^{2n}), E(h, Φ, s) = ∫_{A^∞_{G′}}Σ_{γ∈𝒫′(F)∖G′(F)} Φ(e_{2n}γah)|det(ah)|^s da (Re s > 1; continuation to 𝒯([G′]) with simple poles at 0, 1, residues Φ(0), Φ̂(0), Jacquet–Shalika Lemma 4.2), and for ξ ∈ _PW_{P,2}, ξ ≠ 1, J(ξ, φ, λ, Φ, s) = ∫_{A^∞_{G′}P_ξ̃(F)∖G′(A)} e^{⟨λ,H_P(ξ̃h)⟩}φ(ξ̃h)E(h, Φ, s) dh: there is r > 0 such that on D_r = {Re⟨λ, α^∨⟩ > r} × ℂ ∖ {0, 1} the integral converges absolutely and locally uniformly and is holomorphic; for ξ ≠ ξ_0 it extends holomorphically to D_r × ℂ; for ξ = ξ_0 it has simple poles at s = 0, 1 with residues Φ(0)J(ξ_0, φ, λ) and Φ̂(0)J(ξ_0, φ, λ).
items.note: Uses the bounds (5.2.2.2)–(5.2.2.3) extracted from Jacquet–Lapid–Rogawski (Prop. 24 and after (58)).

items.name: Propositions 5.3.4.1, 5.4.5.1 and Corollary 5.4.5.2: the period of a pseudo-Eisenstein series against the Epstein series
items.statement: For the pseudo-Eisenstein series θ(g) = Σ_{δ∈P(F)∖G(F)} B(δg), B(g) = ∫_{κ+i𝔞^{G,*}_P} e^{⟨λ,H_P(g)⟩}(I_P(λ, f)φ)(g)β(λ) dλ (β Paley–Wiener, f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F_∞)), κ in the convergence range with ⟨κ, α^∨⟩ > r): if β vanishes at −μ_{i,s} (the exponents of the constant term (5.3.1.1)), ∫_{[G′]_0} θ(h)E(h, Φ, s) dh = Σ_{ξ∈_PW_{P,2}, ξ≠1} ∫_{κ+i𝔞^{G,*}_P} J(ξ, I_P(λ, f)φ, λ, Φ, s)β(λ) dλ (5.3.4.1); if β vanishes at ±sα/2, it equals ∫_{κ+i𝔞^{G,*}_P}(∫_{N′_{2n}(A)∖G′(A)} 𝒲(h, I_P(λ, f)φ, λ)Φ(e_{2n}h)|det h|^s dh)β(λ) dλ (5.4.5.1), where 𝒲(g, φ, λ) = W(g, E(φ, λ)) (5.4.3.1). Hence Σ_{ξ≠1} J(ξ, φ, λ, Φ, s) = ∫_{N′_{2n}(A)∖G′(A)} 𝒲(h, φ, λ)Φ(e_{2n}h)|det h|^s dh for Re s ≫ 0 (Corollary 5.4.5.2).
items.note: Unfolding through the variant mirabolics 𝒫_i with the partial Fourier coefficients W_i and the vanishing of constant terms θ_{P_i} for i ∉ {n, 2n} (Lemma 5.4.6.1); Proposition 5.4.4.1 (absolute convergence) uses (5.4.4.2), Beuzart-Plessis's Asai estimates and Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika's bound (1979, Prop. 2.4.1); Lapid–Rogawski Lemma 9.1.2 separates the λ-integrals.

items.name: Lemma 5.5.2.1: local Asai-type integrals of Jacquet integrals of induced generic unitary representations
items.statement: With the Jacquet integral 𝒲_S(g_S, φ_S, λ) (5.4.4.1) and the factorisation 𝒲(g, I_P(λ, f)φ, λ) = L^S(1 + ⟨λ, α^∨⟩, σ × σ^c)^{−1}𝒲_S(g_S, ·, λ)∏_{v∉S}W^ψ_v(g_v, π_λ) (5.4.4.2): (1) there are η, ε > 0 with ∫_{N′_{2n}(F_S)∖𝒫′(F_S)} 𝒲_S(h_S, φ_S, λ) dh_S and ∫_{N′_{2n}(F_S)∖G′(F_S)} 𝒲_S(h_S, φ_S, λ)Φ_S(e_{2n}h_S)|det h_S|^s dh_S absolutely convergent and holomorphic for |⟨Re λ, α^∨⟩| < η (and s ∈ ℋ_{>1−ε}); (2) the latter continues meromorphically to ℂ × 𝔞^{G,*}_{P,ℂ} as Z_S(s, λ, Φ_S); (3) for |⟨Re λ, α^∨⟩| < c and Re s ≥ s_1 it converges absolutely to Z_S.
items.note: Variations on Beuzart-Plessis's Asai paper (Lemmas 3.3.1–3.3.2, §3.10), using that local components of cuspidal representations are generic unitary, hence fully induced from essentially discrete series with exponents in ]−½, ½[ (separate item).

items.name: Classification of irreducible generic unitary representations of GL_n over a local field
items.statement: Every irreducible generic unitary representation of GL_n(F_v) is fully induced from essentially discrete series representations twisted by exponents in ]−½, ½[ (Zelevinsky 1980, Tadić 2009, Badulescu–Renard 2010, Thm. 8.2).
items.note: PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 routes Tadić's description of the generic unitary dual to ET.6 (and Vogan's archimedean one to AF.1); this route coalesces with the ET.6 source, the archimedean case imported from AF.1.

items.name: Theorem 5.5.1.1: the basic intertwining period in terms of the Whittaker functional
items.statement: For λ ∈ i𝔞^{G,*}_{P,ℂ} and S large, with L^{S,*}(1, Π_λ, As) = L^S(1 + ⟨λ, α^∨⟩, σ, As)L^S(1 − ⟨λ, α^∨⟩, σ*, As)L^{S,*}(1, σ × σ^∨): J(ξ_0, φ, λ) = (Δ^{S,*}_{G′})^{−1}L^{S,*}(1, Π_λ, As)∫_{N′_{2n}(F_S)∖𝒫′(F_S)} 𝒲(p_S, φ, λ) dp_S, the integral absolutely convergent; both sides are holomorphic at λ ∈ i𝔞^{G,*}_P if σ is not G′_n-distinguished, or if it is and λ ≠ 0 (where J(ξ_0, ·, λ) may have a simple pole at λ = 0).
items.note: Residue at s = 1 of Corollary 5.4.5.2 against the Epstein series, with Flicker's local computations and Shahidi's non-vanishing of L^S(1 + ⟨λ, α^∨⟩, σ, As^−) (1981, Thm. 5.1); holomorphy of J(ξ_0) for non-distinguished σ from Lapid 2006, Lemma 8.1. Of independent interest: a JLR intertwining period as an integral of a Whittaker functional.

items.name: Hermitian cuspidal data of G_n in the regular case and the Flicker functional β_n on W(Π_λ, ψ_n)
items.statement: Every χ ∈ 𝔛(G_n) is represented by M = ∏_{i∈I}G^{×d_i}_{n_i} × ∏_{j∈J}G^{×d_j}_{n_j} × ∏_{k∈K}G^{×d_k}_{n_k}, π = ⊠_i π^{⊠d_i}_i ⊠ ⊠_j π^{⊠d_j}_j ⊠ ⊠_k π^{⊠d_k}_k with distinct cuspidal π_ℓ, π_i ≄ π*_i (i ∈ I), π_j ≅ π*_j without, and π_k ≅ π*_k with, a pole of L(s, ·, As^{(−1)^{n+1}}) at s = 1; χ is Hermitian iff every i ∈ I has i* with π_{i*} ≅ π*_i and every d_j is even (6.2.3.1). For regular χ all d_ℓ = 1, Hermitian means J = ∅ and i ↦ i* a fixed-point-free involution of I; then L = ∏_{i∈I′}G_{n_i+n_{i*}} × ∏_{k∈K}G_{n_k}. For λ ∈ i𝔞^{L,*}_M: β_n(W) = (Δ^{S,*}_{G′_n})^{−1}L^{S,*}(1, Π, As^{(−1)^{n+1}})∫_{N′_n(F_S)∖𝒫′_n(F_S)} W(p_S)η_{G′_n}(p_S) dp_S on W(Π_λ, ψ_n), convergent and independent of S large.
items.note: Extends the β_n of PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22 from ∗-regular to regular data.

items.name: Theorem 6.2.6.1 and Corollary 6.2.7.1: the Flicker–Rallis period for regular cuspidal data
items.statement: For χ ∈ 𝔛_reg(G_n), f ∈ 𝒞_χ([G_n]) and φ ∈ 𝒮(A^n): (1) if χ is Hermitian, λ ↦ β_n(W_{f,Π_λ}) is Schwartz on i𝔞^{L,*}_M and f ↦ it is continuous 𝒞_χ([G_n]) → 𝒮(i𝔞^{L,*}_M); (2) s ↦ (s − 1)Z^FR_ψ(s, ⁰f, φ) continues analytically to ℋ_{>1} with limit Z^{FR,*}_ψ(1, ⁰f, φ) = 2^{1−dim 𝔞_L}φ̂(0)∫_{i𝔞^{L,*}_M} β_n(W_{f,Π_λ}) dλ if χ is Hermitian and 0 otherwise (6.2.6.2); (3) φ̂(0)P_{G′_n}(f) = ½Z^{FR,*}_ψ(1, ⁰f, φ). Hence P_{G′_n}(f) = 2^{−dim 𝔞_L}∫_{i𝔞^{L,*}_M} β_n(W_{f,Π_λ}) dλ if χ is Hermitian, 0 otherwise.
items.note: The proof follows PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22 §6.3 with the polynomial P(s, x) (6.2.8) and Beuzart-Plessis (Invent. 2021) Lemma 3.11, Prop. 3.12, Lemma 2.16.3; ∗-regularity is replaced by regularity.

items.name: Theorem 6.1.1.1: the second proof of the (G, H)-regular contribution
items.statement: For χ (G, H)-regular and f ∈ 𝒮(G(A)): I_χ(f) = 0 if χ is not Hermitian, and I_χ(f) = 2^{−dim 𝔞_L}∫_{i𝔞^{L,*}_M} I_{Π_λ}(f) dλ if it is (6.1.1.1).
items.note: Via the canonical extension P*_H of the Rankin–Selberg period to 𝒯_χ([G]) (PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22, Thm. 7.1.3.1), Corollary 6.2.7.1 and the spectral expansion (6.3.0.2)–(6.3.0.3) (Lapid's Theorem 2.9.8.1).

items.name: The data 𝔛^h_Π, the base-change map bc and the relative characters J^h_Π(λ, f)
items.statement: For h ∈ ℋ°, 𝔛^h_Π ⊂ 𝔛(U_h) is the set of classes (M_h, σ) with Π a weak base change of (P_h, σ), σ unramified outside S_0 (for ∏_{v∉S_0}(M_h(F_v) ∩ K_{h,v})), and Π_{0,v} the split base change of σ_{0,v} for v ∉ S′_0 ∪ V_{F,∞} (S′_0 = (S_0 ∖ V_{F,∞}) ∪ {inert places}). With M_h = G^♯ × U, bc: 𝔞^{L,*}_M ≅ 𝔞*_{M_h}, the antidiagonal embedding x ↦ (x, −x). J^h_Π(λ, f) = Σ_{(M_h,σ)} J^h_{P_h,σ}(bc(λ), f) over representatives of 𝔛^h_Π (7.1.5.2), absolutely and locally uniformly convergent (Müller, GAFA 1998, Cor. 0.3), holomorphic on i𝔞^{L,*}_M, independent of representatives (Proposition 3.5.5.1).
items.note: Corrected statement: bc pulls the measure on 𝔞*_{M_h} back to 2^{−dim 𝔞^L_M} times the measure on 𝔞^{L,*}_M, as (7.1.7.3) uses; the remark prints 2^{dim 𝔞^L_M} (sourceIssues E8).

items.name: Lemmas 7.1.7.1 and 7.1.7.2: multipliers isolating Π_λ and 𝔛^h_Π
items.statement: For h ∈ ℋ° and λ ∈ i𝔞^{L,*}_M in general position there is μ^h ∈ ℳ^{S′_0}(U_h(A)) such that μ^h ∗ f^h maps L²([U_h]) into ⊕̂_{χ∈𝔛^h_Π} L²_χ([U_h]) and μ^h(Ind^{U_h}_{P_h}(σ_{bc(λ)})) = 1 for (M_h, σ) ∈ 𝔛^h_Π; and there is μ ∈ ℳ^{S′_0}(G(A)) with μ ∗ f mapping L²(G(F)A_G(A)∖G(A)) into L²_{χ_0}([G]) and μ(Π_λ) = 1. The μ^h may be taken as base changes of μ, and μ ∗ f, μ^h ∗ f^h still satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem 7.1.6.1.
items.note: From Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu Theorems 1.3, 3.19, 4.14(1) and 4.14(4), Lemma 4.12 and Proposition 4.8, Ramakrishnan's theorem, Jacquet–Shalika II Thm. 4.4 and the GRS descent. Assertion 2 applies BPLZZ Theorem 4.14(4) to ρ whose base change Π_0 need not be cuspidal (sourceIssues E1); the lead-in cites 'Theorem 3.17' for 3.19 (E10).

items.name: Theorem 7.1.6.1: the global identity of relative characters for H-regular Hermitian parameters
items.statement: Let χ_0 = [(M_P, π)] be (G, H)-regular Hermitian as in §4.1.4, Π = Ind^G_P(π) (with K°-fixed vectors), f ∈ 𝒮°(G(A)) and f^h ∈ 𝒮°(U_h(A)) (h ∈ ℋ°) with (1) f = (Δ^{S_0,*}_HΔ^{S_0,*}_{G′})f_{S_0} ⊗ f^{S_0}, (2) f^h = (Δ^{S_0}_{U′_h})²f^h_{S_0} ⊗ f^{h,S_0}, (3) f_{S_0}, f^h_{S_0} transfers (BPLZZ Def. 4.4), (4) f^{h,S_0} = BC^{S_0}_h(f^{S_0}), (5) f^{S_0} a smooth compactly supported function on ∏′_{v∉S′_0∪V_{F,∞}}G(F_v) times 1_{∏_{v∈S′_0∖S_0}G(O_v)}. Then Σ_{h∈ℋ°} J^h_Π(λ, f^h) = |S_Π|^{−1}I_{P,π}(λ, f) for every λ ∈ i𝔞^{L,*}_M (7.1.6.1).
items.note: Proof: the geometric comparison I(f) = Σ_h J^h(f^h) (Chaudouard–Zydor, Thm. 1.6.1.1) for μ ∗ f and μ^h ∗ f^h, Theorems 3.5.7.1 and 4.1.8.1 to get (7.1.7.3), then separation of λ by spherical Hecke operators at two places of distinct residue characteristic, Stone–Weierstrass, Ramakrishnan and Jacquet–Shalika. For discrete Π it is Proposition 10.1.6.1 of PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22.

items.name: Local relative characters for induced tempered representations and the factorisation of I_{Q,π}(λ, f)
items.statement: For σ tempered on M_P(A) with strong base change π (Mok, KMSW), Π = Ind^G_Q(π) and λ ∈ i𝔞*_Π: J_{Σ_{λ,v}}(f^h_v) = ∫_{U′_h(F_v)} Trace(Σ_{λ,v}(h_v)Σ_{λ,v}(f^h_v)) dh_v (absolutely convergent, Harris) with J_{Σ_{λ,v}}(1_{U_h(O_v)}) = Δ^{−2}_{U′_h,v}L(½, Π_{λ,v})/L(1, Π_{λ,v}, As′) for v ∉ S_0; I_{Π_{λ,v}}(f_v) = Σ_{W_v} α_v(Π_v(f_v)W_v)\overline{β_{η,v}(W_v)}/⟨W_v, W_v⟩_{Whitt,v} with α_v(W) = ∫_{N_H(F_v)∖H(F_v)} W, β_{η,v}, ⟨·,·⟩_{Whitt,v} as before (absolutely convergent by temperedness, JPSS Prop. 8.4); and I_{Q,π}(λ, f) = L^{S_0}(½, Π_λ)/L^{S_0,*}(1, Π_λ, As′)∏_{v∈S_0} I_{Π_{λ,v}}(f_v) for f = Δ^{S_0,*}_HΔ^{S_0,*}_{G′}∏_{v∈S_0}f_v × ∏_{v∉S_0}1_{G(O_v)} (7.3.2.1).
items.note: The theorem is reduced to (7.3.1.1), J^h_{P,σ}(λ, f^h) = |S_Π|^{−1}L^{S_0}(½, Π_λ)/L^{S_0,*}(1, Π_λ, As′)∏_{v∈S_0} J_{Σ_{λ,v}}(f^h_v); the star is missing in the print (sourceIssues E9).

items.name: Beuzart-Plessis's comparison of local relative characters for induced tempered representations
items.statement: If Π_v is the local base change of σ_v (tempered) and f_v, f^h_v are transfers, then I_{Π_{λ,v}}(f_v) = κ_vJ_{Σ_{λ,v}}(f^h_v) with explicit κ_v ∈ ℂ^×, ∏_{v∈S_0}κ_v = 1 (Beuzart-Plessis, Invent. Math. 2021, Thm. 5.4.1) (7.3.4.2).
items.note: Already in this candidate (BPLZZ Lemma 4.9, PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22); used here for induced representations.

items.name: Mok and Kaletha–Mínguez–Shin–White: strong base change of tempered cuspidal representations of Levi subgroups of unitary groups
items.statement: A cuspidal σ of M_P(A) ⊂ U_h(A), tempered everywhere, has a strong base change π to M_Q, Q = Res_{E/F}(P_E) (local base change at every place, as defined by Mok and KMSW), so π and Ind^G_Q(π) are tempered everywhere; cuspidal representations of U_h are described by local L-packets.
items.note: The endoscopic classification of unitary groups is ML.4.

items.name: Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry descent (existence of a unitary datum with base change Π)
items.statement: For an H-regular Hermitian Arthur parameter Π there is h♭ ∈ ℋ° with 𝔛^{h♭}_Π ≠ ∅; for m = 0 the GRS descent also proves the Whittaker case of Theorem 1.3.3.1.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 7.1.7.1, p. 66, and Remarks 1.3.3.2, p. 7
items.note: Automorphic descent is ML.5.

items.name: Existence of transfer and positivity of unitary relative characters
items.statement: Test functions f, (f^h) satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem 7.1.6.1 with prescribed non-vanishing of either side exist (p-adic transfer, W. Zhang, Ann. of Math. 2014; archimedean approximation, Xue 2019), and J^{h_0}_{P,σ}(bc(λ), ξ ∗ ξ^∨) ≥ 0 with strict positivity for the chosen σ_0 (Zhang, p. 993).
items.note: The same inputs as in PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22, applied to Eisenstein data.

items.name: The auxiliary groups of the reduction to corank one
items.statement: With h_m ∈ ℋ_m, h_{m+1} = h_m ⊕ h_0, h_n = h^{⊕r}_s ⊕ h_m, h_{n+1} = h_n ⊕ h_0 and U_m ⊂ U_{m+1} ⊂ U_n ⊂ U_{n+1}: 𝒢 = U_m × U_{n+1}, U = U_n × U_{n+1}, Ũ = U_m × U_{m+1}; ℬ = U_m ⋉ N, U′ = U_n, Ũ′ = U_m (8.1.3.2); P′ = P ∩ U_n; Q_n ⊂ U_n and Q_{n+1} ⊂ U_{n+1} the stabilisers of X_r with unipotent radicals V_n, V_{n+1}; G_r ⊂ U_n, U_{n+1} acting on X_r, Y_r; N = N_r ⋉ V_{n+1}; L_n = G_r × U_m (8.1.3.3); Q = Q_n × U_{n+1}, L = L_n × U_{n+1} = G_r × 𝒢; ℬ_L = N_r × ℬ with ψ^L_ℬ = ψ_{−r} ⊠ ψ_ℬ; ℬ′ = U′ ∩ ℬ_L = (N_r × U_m) ⋉ V_n; Eisenstein series E^{U_n}_{Q_n}(φ_n, s) and hyperspecial maximal compacts outside S.
items.note: The coordinates in which a Bessel period of U_m × U_{n+1} becomes a Whittaker–Bessel period of a Levi of U_n × U_{n+1}.

items.name: Measures on N_k and G_k, the constants ν(G_{k,v}) and the mirabolic Fourier inversion formula
items.statement: d_{ψ_v} is the ψ_v-self-dual measure on E_v; N_k(F_v) gets ∏_{i<j} d_{ψ_v}u_{ij} (product the Tamagawa measure, vol[N_k] = 1); d_{ψ_v}g_v = ∏d_{ψ_v}g_{ij}/|det g_v|^k_{E_v}; ν(G_{k,v}) = dg_v(d_{ψ_v}g_v)^{−1}; Δ*_{G_k} = ζ*_E(1)∏_{i=2}^kζ_E(i), vol(K_{k,v}, d_{ψ_v}g_v) = Δ^{−1}_{G_k,v} at unramified v, and ∏_{v∈T}ν(G_{k,v}) = (Δ^{T,*}_{G_k})^{−1} (8.2.1.1). For f ∈ C_c^∞(𝒫_{k+1}(F_v)) with W_f(g_1, g_2) = ∫_{N_{k+1}(F_v)} f(g_1^{−1}ug_2)ψ_{k+1}(u) du: f(p) = ν(G_{k,v})^{−1}∫_{N_k(F_v)∖G_k(F_v)} W_f(γ, γp) dγ (8.2.2.1).
items.note: The Tamagawa measures themselves are AA.2; the inversion formula is the Whittaker–Plancherel identity for the mirabolic subgroup.

items.name: Whittaker, Bessel and mixed Whittaker–Bessel global periods
items.statement: 𝒫_{N_r,ψ_{−r}}(φ) = ∫_{[N_r]} φ(u)ψ_{−r}(u) du on 𝒜([G_r]); 𝒫_{ℬ,ψ_ℬ} on 𝒜([𝒢]) and 𝒫_{U′} on 𝒜([U]) where convergent (e.g. φ_n ⊗ φ_{n+1} with φ_{n+1} cuspidal); 𝒫_{ℬ_L,ψ^L_ℬ}(φ) = ∫_{[ℬ_L]} φψ^L_ℬ on 𝒜([L]), equal to 𝒫_{N_r,ψ_{−r}}(φ_r)𝒫_{ℬ,ψ_ℬ}(φ′) for φ = φ_r ⊗ φ′ with φ′ cuspidal.
items.note: The mixed period of the Levi L of Q.

items.name: Proposition 8.5.1.1: global unfolding of the U′-period of an Eisenstein series
items.statement: For φ_n ∈ 𝒜_{Q_n}(U_n) and φ_{n+1} ∈ 𝒜_cusp(U_{n+1}) there is c > 0 with 𝒫_{U′}(E^{U_n}_{Q_n}(φ_n, s) ⊗ φ_{n+1}) = ∫_{ℬ′(A)∖U′(A)} 𝒫_{ℬ_L,ψ^L_ℬ}(R(h)(φ_{n,s} ⊗ φ_{n+1})) dh for s ∈ ℋ_{>c}, absolutely convergent.
items.note: Uses the Fourier expansion of the cusp form φ_{n+1,V_n} along the mirabolic 𝒫_{r+1} (Cogdell, §1.1) and the decay of Fourier coefficients (PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22, Lemma 2.6.1.1).

items.name: Proposition 8.6.1.1 and Lemma 8.6.1.2: local unfolding of Whittaker–Bessel functionals
items.statement: For irreducible τ, σ_m, σ_{n+1} of G_r(F_v), U_m(F_v), U_{n+1}(F_v) and L ∈ Hom_{ℬ_L(F_v)}(τ ⊠ σ, ψ^L_{ℬ,v}): L^{U′}_s(φ_{n,s} ⊗ φ_{n+1}) = ∫_{ℬ′(F_v)∖U′(F_v)} L(φ_{n,s}(h) ⊗ σ_{n+1}(h)φ_{n+1}) dh converges for Re s > c (c = −½ if σ and τ are tempered), and for Re s ≫ 0, L ≢ 0 iff L^{U′}_s ≢ 0 on I^{U_n}_{Q_n}(τ_s ⊠ σ_m) ⊗ σ_{n+1}. Lemma 8.6.1.2: |L((τ(a) ⊗ σ(a))φ)| ≪_R ‖a‖^{−R}_{E^r_v}‖a‖^D, and ≪_R ‖a‖^{−R}Ξ^{G_r}(a)Ξ^{U_{n+1}}(a) in the tempered case, for a ∈ T_r(F_v).
items.note: After Beuzart-Plessis, Astérisque 418, Lemma B.2.1 and Lemma 7.3.1(i), Waldspurger's Ξ-bounds (2003, Lemme II.1.1) and the surjectivity of the Kirillov model (separate item).

items.name: The Kirillov model of generic representations of GL_r
items.statement: For τ an irreducible generic representation of G_r(F_v) with Whittaker functional L_W, every f ∈ C_c^∞(N_{r−1}(F_v)∖G_{r−1}(F_v)) is h ↦ L_W(τ(h)φ_τ) for some φ_τ ∈ τ (Gelfand–Kazhdan 1975, Thm. 6; Kemarsky 2015, Thm. 1 at complex places).
items.note: Local GL_n Whittaker theory; the p-adic case belongs with SR.5's Bernstein–Zelevinsky derivatives and the archimedean case with AL.3's archimedean Whittaker API.

items.name: Proposition 8.6.2.1 and Lemma 8.6.2.2: the local U′-period as a double Whittaker–Bessel integral
items.note: Absolute convergence from Cowling–Haagerup–Howe (Thm. 2), Waldspurger (Lemme II.1.6) and BP20 Lemma 6.5.1; the identity reduces to (8.2.2.1).

items.name: Proposition 8.7.2.1: the unramified computation of the local unfolding
items.statement: For v ∉ S, τ, σ_m, σ_{n+1} unramified and spherical φ°_{n,s}, φ°_{n+1}, for Re s ≫ 0: L^{U′}_s(φ°_{n,s} ⊗ φ°_{n+1}) = vol(K^U_{n,v})/vol(K^U_{n,v} ∩ ℬ′(F_v)) · L(½ + s, τ × σ_{n+1})/(L(1 + s, τ^c × σ_m)L(1 + 2s, τ, As^{(−1)^m})) · L(φ°_{n,s}(1) ⊗ φ°_{n+1}) (8.7.2.1).
items.note: Proof by Shintani and Casselman–Shalika for L_W, the Khoury–Liu–Zhang formula for L_B (Lemma 8.7.2.2), the Cauchy identity (Lemma 8.7.2.3) and the twisted Weyl character formula of Appendix A applied to the identity (8.7.2.8), whose right side is shown independent of S_{n+1} by a dot-action argument. An inaccuracy in a previous version was pointed out by P. Boisseau (Acknowledgements).

items.name: Shintani and Casselman–Shalika: unramified Whittaker functions of GL_r
items.statement: For unramified generic τ with spherical φ°_τ and L_W(φ°_τ) = 1: L_W(τ(t)φ°_τ) = δ_{B_r}(t)^{1/2}ch_t(S_τ) for t ∈ Λ^+_r and 0 otherwise (8.7.2.3), ch_t the character of the irreducible representation of ^LG_r of highest weight χ_t.
items.note: The unramified Whittaker computation underlying AL.3's unramified Rankin–Selberg calculations; the ^LG_r-character form is the consumer's bookkeeping.

items.name: The Cauchy identity for GL_r characters (Lemma 8.7.2.3)
items.statement: For S_1, S_2 ∈ T̂_r Frob_v and Re s ≫ 0: Σ_{t∈Λ^{++}_r}|det t|^{½+s}_{E_v}ch_t(S_1)ch_t(S_2) = det(1 − q^{−1/2}S_{1,s} ⊗^I S_2)^{−1}, S_{1,s} = q^{−s}S_1 (from Bump, Lie Groups, Thm. 43.3).
items.note: The Cauchy identity Σ_λ s_λ(x)s_λ(y) = ∏(1 − x_iy_j)^{−1} is planned in Tau Ceti's SchurWeyl (via RSK) and the identification of GL_n characters with Schur polynomials in ClassicalGroups; the L-group reformulation is part of Proposition 8.7.2.1.

items.name: Proposition 8.8.2.1 and (8.8.1.1): non-vanishing of Bessel periods via Eisenstein periods
items.statement: For σ_m, σ_{n+1} cuspidal and τ induced from a unitary cuspidal representation of a Levi of G_r (τ = {E^{G_r}_R(φ, 0)}), σ_n = I^{U_n}_{Q_n}(τ ⊠ σ_m): 𝒫_{U′}(E^{U_n}_{Q_n}(φ_n, s) ⊗ φ_{n+1}) = [vol ratio]·L^T(½ + s, τ × σ_{n+1})/(L^T(1 + s, τ^c × σ_m)L^T(1 + 2s, τ, As^{(−1)^m}))·∫_{ℬ′(F_T)∖U′(F_T)} 𝒫_{ℬ_L,ψ^L_ℬ}(φ_{n,s}(h) ⊗ σ_{n+1}(h)φ_{n+1}) dh (8.8.1.1) for Re s ≫ 0; and 𝒫_{ℬ,ψ_ℬ} ≢ 0 on σ_m ⊠ σ_{n+1} iff 𝒫_{U′}(E^{U_n}_{Q_n}(φ_n, s) ⊗ φ_{n+1}) ≠ 0 for some φ_n, φ_{n+1} and some s where E^{U_n}_{Q_n}(φ_n, ·) is regular.
items.note: Combines Propositions 8.5.1.1, 8.6.1.1 and 8.7.2.1 with the non-vanishing of the Whittaker period on τ.

items.name: Proposition 8.8.3.1: the refined identity for Bessel periods from that for Eisenstein periods
items.statement: With Petersson products on σ_m, σ_{n+1}, the inner product ⟨E(φ, 0), E(φ′, 0)⟩_τ = ∫_{R(A)∖G_r(A)}∫_{[M]^1} φ(mg)\overline{φ′(mg)} on τ, the induced product on σ_n, their local factorisations, and the regularised products ∏′_v of local periods (with L^{T,*}(1, σ_n, Ad), L^{T,*}(1, τ, Ad) the leading coefficients of order a = dim A_M): if |𝒫_{U′}(E^{U_n}_{Q_n}(φ_n, s) ⊗ φ_{n+1})|² = c∏′_v 𝒫_{U′,v}(φ_{n,s,v} ⊗ φ_{n+1,v}, ·) for all factorisable vectors and s ∈ iℝ, then |𝒫_{ℬ,ψ_ℬ}(φ_m ⊗ φ_{n+1})|² = c∏′_v 𝒫_{ℬ,ψ_ℬ,v}(φ_{m,v} ⊗ φ_{n+1,v}, ·) for all factorisable φ_m, φ_{n+1}.
items.note: Divides (8.8.3.3) by the Whittaker-period factorisation |𝒫_{N_r,ψ_{−r}}(φ_τ)|² = ∏′_v𝒫_{N_r,ψ_{−r},v}(φ_{τ,v}, φ_{τ,v}) (separate item), using Proposition 8.6.2.1, (8.2.1.1) and the unramified local values of Liu and Harris.

items.name: Factorisation of the Whittaker period of an induced representation of GL_r
items.statement: For τ induced from a unitary cuspidal representation, |𝒫_{N_r,ψ_{−r}}(φ_τ)|² = ∏′_v 𝒫_{N_r,ψ_{−r},v}(φ_{τ,v}, φ_{τ,v}) with the regularised product (Δ^{T,*}_{G_r}/L^{T,*}(1, τ, Ad))∏_{v∈T} (Feigon–Lapid–Offen, (11.3)); unramified local values P_{N_r,ψ_{−r},v}(φ_{τ,v}, φ_{τ,v}) = Δ_{G_r,v}/L(1, τ_v, Ad).
items.note: The Whittaker-period counterpart of the Petersson–Whittaker identity of PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22 (Thm. 8.1.2.1).

items.name: The Borel–Weil–Bott theorem
items.statement: For a connected complex reductive Ĝ with Borel B̂ ⊃ T̂, X = Ĝ/B̂ and the Ĝ-equivariant line bundle ℒ_χ attached to χ ∈ X*(T̂): if χ + ρ is singular, H^i(X, ℒ_χ) = 0 for all i; otherwise exactly one H^i(X, ℒ_χ) is non-zero and it is isomorphic to V_{χ^+}, χ^+ = w_χ·χ dominant (dot action w·χ = w(χ + ρ) − ρ).
items.locator: Appendix A, proof of Proposition A.0.2.1, p. 95
items.note: Tau Ceti's LieGroups Layer 8 plans Borel–Weil with 'the Borel–Weil–Bott extension (higher cohomology and non-dominant λ) stated as its refinement'.

items.name: The Atiyah–Bott holomorphic Lefschetz fixed point formula
items.statement: For a holomorphic automorphism S of a compact complex manifold X with isolated non-degenerate fixed points, lifted to a holomorphic line bundle ℒ: Σ_i(−1)^iTr(S | H^i(X, ℒ)) = Σ_{S(x)=x} Tr(S | ℒ_x)/det(1 − dS_x^{−1} | T^{1,0}_xX) (Atiyah–Bott, Ann. of Math. 88 (1968), Thm. 4.12), applied to regular S ∈ T̂F acting on Ĝ/B̂ with fixed points W ⊂ X.
items.locator: Appendix A, proof of Proposition A.0.2.1, p. 95
items.note: A cited input for the twisted character formula.

items.name: Proposition A.0.2.1: Weyl's character formula for non-connected groups ^LG = Ĝ ⋊ Γ
items.statement: Let Γ be finite cyclic acting holomorphically on Ĝ preserving (B̂, T̂), ^LG = Ĝ ⋊ Γ, ^LT = T̂ ⋊ Γ, W = Norm_Ĝ(^LT)/T̂ = Ŵ^Γ, D_{Ĝ/B̂}(S) = det(1 − Ad(S) | Lie Ĝ/Lie B̂), and for dominant Γ-invariant χ let ch_χ be the character of the unique extension of V_χ to ^LG with Γ trivial on the highest weight line. For a generator F of Γ and χ ∈ X*(T̂)^Γ: (1) if χ + ρ is singular, Σ_{w∈W}χ(wS)/D_{Ĝ/B̂}(wS) = 0 for every regular S ∈ ^LT; (2) otherwise, with χ^+ = w_χ·χ (w_χ ∈ W), there is a root of unity ε_χ with Σ_{w∈W}χ(wS)/D_{Ĝ/B̂}(wS) = ε_χ ch_{χ^+}(S) for regular S ∈ T̂F, and ε_χ = 1 if χ is dominant.
items.locator: Appendix A, A.0.1–A.0.2, Proposition A.0.2.1, pp. 94–95
items.note: Proved from Borel–Weil–Bott and the Atiyah–Bott fixed point formula on Ĝ/B̂ = ^LG/^LB.

items.name: Corollary A.0.2.2: the Weyl denominator sum over a Levi
items.statement: For a Γ-stable standard parabolic Q̂ ⊃ B̂ with Levi L̂ ⊃ T̂ and W_L = Norm_{^LL}(T̂)/T̂: Σ_{w∈W_L}D_{Ĝ/B̂}(wS)^{−1} = D_{Ĝ/Q̂}(S)^{−1} for every regular S ∈ ^LT.
items.note: From D_{Ĝ/B̂} = D_{Ĝ/Q̂}D_{L̂/B̂_L} and Proposition A.0.2.1 for the trivial character of ^LL.

items.name: Eisenstein series and intertwining operators on unitary groups and on G_n
items.statement: For φ ∈ 𝒜_{P,cusp}(G) and Q ⊃ P, E^Q(g, φ, λ) = Σ_{δ∈P(F)∖Q(F)} e^{⟨λ,H_P(δg)⟩}φ(δg) (2.2.4.1) converges for Re λ in a cone and continues meromorphically; intertwining operators M(w, λ): 𝒜_P(G) → 𝒜_Q(G) with the functional equations E(φ, λ) = E(M(w, λ)φ, wλ).
items.note: Induced families, Eisenstein series and intertwining operators are AS.1–AS.2 (smooth forms as in PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22).

items.name: Automorphic forms, cuspidal data and the Langlands decomposition (preliminaries)
items.statement: 𝒜_P(G) = 𝒵(𝔤_∞)-finite functions in 𝒯([G]_P), cusp forms (φ_Q = 0 for Q ⊊ P), cuspidal representations and inductions 𝒜_{P,π,cusp}(G) with Petersson norm, normalised central characters, K-bases; 𝔛(G) and L²([G]_P) = ⊕̂_{χ∈𝔛(G)}L²_χ([G]_P) with kernels K_{f,P,χ}; Haar and Tamagawa measures and heights as in PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22.
items.note: Automorphic forms and constant terms are AF.2–AF.3, the L²-decomposition AS.4, measures AA.2.
